usage: fleet-switchboard launch [-h] [--agent AGENT] [--dir DIR]
                                [--resume SESSION] [--headless] [--terminal]
                                [--workspace WORKSPACE] [--role ROLE]
                                [--reports-to REPORTS_TO] [--issue ISSUE]
                                [--repo REPO] [--new-workspace LABEL]
                                [--charter CHARTER] [--checkpoint WHEN]
                                [--overdue WHEN] [--brief-file BRIEF_FILE]
                                [--memory-ok REASON] [--cloud]
                                [--branch BRANCH] [--idle IDLE] [--hard HARD]
                                [--shape SHAPE] [--stack]
                                name

Start a fleet agent (headless by default, or in a new herdr tab with
--terminal), without typing. A NEW launch (not a resume or --cloud) first runs
the memory test: this is the lanes' safety check, not the owner's rule (there
are no caps on coders), and `--memory-ok <reason>` overrides it. A refusal
exits 5.

positional arguments:
  name                  The agent's fleet name (lower case, digits, - and _)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent AGENT         The OpenCode agent definition, such as coder
  --dir DIR             The agent's working directory (absolute)
  --resume SESSION      Open a tab on this existing session of NAME instead of
                        creating one (a restart that keeps the conversation)
  --headless            Start the worker with NO terminal: a session in the
                        OpenCode service, the brief sent through the API
                        (about 2 MB instead of a terminal's 200 to 400 MB).
                        Its tools run in the service's environment. The
                        default of a plain launch (see --terminal); unlike the
                        default, an explicit --headless never falls back to a
                        terminal
  --terminal            Open a herdr tab for the worker (a plain launch is
                        headless unless the configuration key launch_default
                        is terminal). Cannot be combined with --headless;
                        --workspace and --new-workspace imply it
  --workspace WORKSPACE
                        The herdr workspace for the new tab (default: the
                        workspace of this session, else $HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID)
  --role ROLE           metadata.fleet.role
  --reports-to REPORTS_TO
                        metadata.fleet.reports_to
  --issue ISSUE         metadata.fleet.issue (owner/repo#N also sets --repo)
  --repo REPO           metadata.fleet.repo, OWNER/REPO: the project the agent
                        works in. Its gh account (config gh_users) is the
                        agent's GH_TOKEN
  --new-workspace LABEL
                        Create a herdr workspace with this label in --dir
                        (never focused), and launch into it. A --charter whose
                        `workspace:` line differs is refused
  --charter CHARTER     metadata.fleet.charter: an orchestrator's charter
                        issue
  --checkpoint WHEN     Remind the worker to report at this time (30m, or an
                        ISO time with a zone). Default: read from the brief's
                        CHECKPOINT line, if it can be
  --overdue WHEN        Wake --reports-to at this time if the worker has not
                        reported since the launch (60m, or an ISO time with a
                        zone)
  --brief-file BRIEF_FILE
                        The first prompt: a file, or - for stdin
  --memory-ok REASON    Skip the memory test of a new launch (audited with the
                        reason)
  --cloud               Run the worker in the cloud (needs --repo and
                        --branch; --dir is its path in the pod, default /work;
                        the pod always runs its own 'worker' agent: --agent is
                        only recorded)
  --branch BRANCH       With --cloud: the branch the worker starts on
  --idle IDLE           With --cloud: stop after this long idle (default 10m)
  --hard HARD           With --cloud: stop after this long whatever it does
                        (default 2h)
  --shape SHAPE         With --cloud: the pod shape, S (2 CPU, 4 GiB; the
                        launcher's default) or M (4 CPU, 8 GiB)
  --stack               With --cloud: a pod that can run a nested Docker stack
                        (the Sysbox runtime class, its own user namespace, no
                        capability added, no privileged mode). Off by default;
                        the launch without it is unchanged. The first pod on a
                        fresh node may wait for the node's runtime: the
                        launcher retries

usage: fleet-switchboard labels [-h] {ensure,apply-from-markers} ...

`labels ensure` creates the labels the fleet uses, each with the repo's own gh
account, unless they exist: <user>:orchestrator, <user>:awaiting-cos and
<user>:awaiting-user. Idempotent. Run it when a repo joins.

positional arguments:
  {ensure,apply-from-markers}
    ensure              Create the missing labels (every watched repo by
                        default)
    apply-from-markers  Label the open PRs and issues whose first body line
                        says MERGE: captain|automatic (a person's command; a
                        dry run unless --apply)

  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

usage: fleet-switchboard heavy [-h] [--slots SLOTS] [--wait-max WAIT_MAX]
                               [--short] [--ceiling CEILING] [--name NAME]
                               ...

`heavy [--slots N] [--wait-max SECONDS] [--short] [--name WHO] --
<command...>`: waits for a free slot in arrival order (default 3, config
`heavy.slots`; one line every 30 s says your place and who holds them), then
runs the command as `taskpolicy -b <command>` (else `nice -n 10`) with its
stdin, stdout, exit status and signals passed through. After --wait-max
seconds (default 1800) it exits 75 and does not run the command.

positional arguments:
  command              -- <command...>

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --slots SLOTS        How many commands may run at once (default: config
                       heavy.slots, else 3)
  --wait-max WAIT_MAX  Give up after this many seconds without a slot: exit 75
                       (default 1800)
  --short              The command is short: when the ordinary slots are busy
                       it may use the one express slot, and the wrapper stops
                       it after 120 seconds (exit 124)
  --ceiling CEILING    Ask for a longer (or shorter) time ceiling in seconds
                       than the kind of command's default, up to the hard
                       maximum (14400); 0 reads as the maximum, an unreadable
                       value as the default
  --name NAME          Who the slot is held for (default: FLEET_HEAVY_NAME,
                       the OpenCode session id, the user)

usage: fleet-switchboard impact [-h] {floor,matrix,hold,delegated,clear} ...

positional arguments:
  {floor,matrix,hold,delegated,clear}
    floor               What the path-glob floor (and an optional independent
                        rating) would decide for a PR
    matrix              Read-only: print the kit's impact matrix words
                        (severities, probabilities, cells, floor rule ids);
                        with --for-rater also a pull request's floor hits (for
                        a repository with no review laws)
    hold                What the daemon would label as held right now (read-
                        only dry run; the daemon writes the labels)
    delegated           List every clear the Chief of Staff made under an
                        order of the owner's: the pull request, head, score,
                        threshold and her judgement (read-only)
    clear               The owner's own terminal: clear a false impact hold
                        for this head, with a reason (the Chief of Staff only
                        under a standing order of the owner's, with --under-
                        order)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

usage: fleet-switchboard install [-h] [--opencode OPENCODE] [--no-service]
                                 [--with-cloud-reaper] [--no-herdr-link]
                                 [--shared-profile] [--profile DIR]
                                 [--gh-user NAME] [--dry-run] [--uninstall]

Idempotent. Each step says done, already done, or skipped (why). Finds an
OpenCode v2 binary (never assumes `opencode` is v2), writes the config keys
that are missing, puts the kit's agents, skills and plugins into a private v2
profile (never the directory your ordinary OpenCode reads, unless --shared-
profile), links the herdr plugin, installs a service that keeps the daemon
alive, then starts the daemon and prints `status`. No secret is written
anywhere.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --opencode OPENCODE  The OpenCode v2 binary (absolute path); default: the
                       configured one, then the known places
  --no-service         Do not install the service
  --with-cloud-reaper  Also install and load the cloud worker reaper as a
                       service (opt-in: it needs a cluster login; its non-
                       secret CW_* settings are copied from this environment)
  --no-herdr-link      Do not link herdr's plugin (it starts the daemon
                       whenever herdr starts)
  --shared-profile     Put v2's pieces in the directory your ordinary OpenCode
                       reads too (~/.config/opencode), which can break a v1
                       OpenCode that reads them. Default: a private profile
  --profile DIR        The private profile's directory (absolute); default:
                       $XDG_DATA_HOME/fleet-switchboard/profile
  --gh-user NAME       The gh account the agents' token comes from (default:
                       gh's active one)
  --dry-run            Print every step; write nothing
  --uninstall          Reverse the profile pieces, the herdr link and the
                       service; config, state and sessions stay

usage: fleet-switchboard job [-h] {start,status} ...

A restart can kill a background run silently. `job start NAME -- COMMAND...`
runs it detached in its own session and records it under the shared temp dir
(or $FLEET_JOBS_DIR); `job status NAME` prints one line: alive, finished (with
its exit code and the result file) or dead (killed, no exit code). A job found
dead that nobody asked about is reported once to its starter's boss.

positional arguments:
  {start,status}
    start         Start a command detached and record it
    status        One line: alive, finished (exit code, result file) or dead
                  (killed, no exit code)

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit

usage: fleet-switchboard labels apply-from-markers [-h] [--repo OWNER/REPO]
                                                   [--dry-run | --apply]

Lists the open PRs and issues of the watched repos (or --repo) whose first
non-empty body line says `MERGE: captain` or `MERGE: automatic` and which
carry NO merge label, and prints what would change. Without --apply nothing is
written (the default, same as --dry-run). With --apply it ensures the labels
exist and adds `<user>:merge-captain` / `<user>:merge-automatic` with the
repo's own gh account, audited. It is a person's command: the daemon never
runs it, and the sweep and triage still write nothing.

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --repo OWNER/REPO  Only this repo
  --dry-run          Print what would change and write nothing (the default)
  --apply            Add the labels
